sources.entry: notebook - A web-based notebook environment for interactive computing.

summary.one_liner: Jupyter Notebook is a web-based, language-agnostic notebook environment for interactive computing, maintained in the jupyter/notebook repository.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Jupyter Notebook as a web-based notebook environment for interactive computing. It states that the project maintains two major versions: Notebook v7, built on JupyterLab frontend components and the Jupyter Server backend, and Classic Notebook v6, which uses nbclassic for its HTML/JavaScript/CSS assets and now receives only maintenance and security fixes. Notebook v5 is no longer maintained. Installation is covered by external ReadTheDocs documentation, and the README gives pip install notebook and jupyter notebook as the basic local install and launch commands. Language-specific kernels live in separate repositories, so this repo focuses on the language-agnostic notebook application. The README also points to a development setup guide in CONTRIBUTING.md.
use_cases: run interactive Python notebooks in a browser
edit and execute code cells with markdown and output
serving notebooks on a remote machine
notable: Notebook v7 is built on JupyterLab frontend components and Jupyter Server
Language-agnostic design; language kernels are separate projects
Classic Notebook v6 maintained on the 6.5.x branch for fixes only
Part of Project Jupyter, originally split from IPython 3
caveats: Notebook v5 is no longer maintained, and v5 or Classic v6 extensions are not compatible with Notebook v7
Upgrading to Notebook v7 may require work if custom extensions are used
